alignment.about: Where a cell's words sit against a row taller than one line. It tells nothing apart on a table of single lines, so this one carries a note that wraps.
alignment.title: Alignment

bridgeNote: Held for a customs count, released on the second of the month
caption: Payouts raised this quarter

corners.about: Every corner of the surface a table sits on.
corners.title: Corners

gathered.about: Rows gathered into a section per heading, and a table holding nothing at all. A section is a `tbody` of its own and its heading states `rowgroup` as its scope, so the rows under it answer to it rather than the columns.
gathered.title: Sections and an empty table

layouts.about: Columns sized to their contents, and columns sharing the width evenly. A fixed layout is what a table needs before its columns can be held still while it scrolls.
layouts.title: Layouts

looks.about: Both looks at every size. A table is read rather than looked at, so the size is the decision that matters most.
looks.title: Looks and sizes

quarters.about: A name that spans the columns under it, over a second row naming each one. A spanning name states `colgroup` as its scope rather than `col`, which is what tells a screen reader that every column beneath answers to it.
quarters.title: Names that span columns

ruled.about: The rules a table is drawn with: between the rows, between the columns as well, or none at all. The rule under the column names is drawn whichever way the rest are.
ruled.title: Rules

rows.about: Rows as they are, striped, and responding to a pointer. A stripe helps an eye track across a wide table and fights the hover on a narrow one.
rows.title: Rows

runs.about: A name that spans the rows under it, for a table of several records per account. A spanning name states `rowgroup` as its scope, and the rule between the groups is what a reader counts by.
runs.title: Names that span rows

stickyBoth.about: Both held at once. The corner cell sits at the crossing of the two and is held in each direction, so it covers whatever passes under it rather than letting the two scrolls meet in it.
stickyBoth.title: Both held at once

stickyColumn.about: A table wider than its box, with each week's own name held as the figures scroll sideways. A reader who has scrolled to September still knows which week they are reading.
stickyColumn.title: The first column held

stickyHeader.about: A table longer than its box, with the column names held as the figures scroll under them. The box is held to a height and the table is laid out fixed: a header sticks within the box that scrolls, so there has to be a height before there is anything to stick to.
stickyHeader.title: The column names held

title: Table
